items.title: Stanley Kay interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001
items.q: So they wrote a book for him, The Drum Book, Henry Aller.

ctx.x: Okay we are in Ohio. And I’d sit next to him on the bus see. Right here. And then he had the outside, I had the window. But you know you’re doing 200 miles and you’ve got to —ah you’re disturbing me. I said, “wait a minute, you don’t want me to breathe?” Because I’d get into that with him. So we get into a town at eight in the morning, in Ohio. Columbus, Ohio. He said, “come on, let’s go to a movie.” He loved movies. Cowboy movies, D movies, E movies, Z’s, whatever they were. I said, “I’m not going to the movies…

act and I played. They see the big sling. Clark Terry told me, he said he was there and the word went out that Buddy’s arm is not broken, he wants to show he can play with one hand. But it was broken. So we played there a week, then we go into the Paramount Theater downtown and the managing director of the Paramount, Bob Whiteman, came up. And he said, “the rumor is that your arm is not broken but there’s a sensation — keep it in the sling.” If it’s not broken we could play the Paramount. See and he never liked…
He was never at a loss, was he?
